author: Jim Ehmke
title: Six dilapidated Binghamton buildings to be demolished - NewsBreak
text:
By Jim Ehmke ,
7 hours ago
BINGHAMTON, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) – Meanwhile, the Land Bank has approved plans to tear down six of the worst blighted buildings in Binghamton. The half dozen residences have been plagued by fires, neglect and squatters.
Some of the worst of the worst begins with 8 Matis St. in the city’s First Ward. It’s the final building left on the narrow dead-end street. The three-story apartment building is located behind Saint Michael’s Church.
There are several fire-damaged buildings on the list. Griswold St. on the Eastside has been vacant since March 2021. According to WNBF, the early-morning blaze was reported at around 4:00 a.m. in the four-apartment building, displacing 11 residents.
37 Munsell St. is a boarded up, dilapidated building with its roof collapsing in a neighborhood that’s being rejuvenated. It’s currently surrounded by recent new low-income housing developments created by Greater Opportunities of Broome and Chenango. The Land Bank says it’s offering to sell the property to the organization as well.
49 Rush Ave. on the Southside has been vacant since a fire there in October 2023 that badly damaged the second floor. No one was injured in the fire. A sign posted on the building indicates that the city has condemned it.
124 Walnut St. was once home to A Schaad Appliances and sits across the street from Walnut Street Park. Neighbors say it’s been vacant for the last several years and has become a haven for drug addicts and vagrants.
Next door, 51 Gerard Ave. was originally owned by the Schaad family. Neighbors say squatters have been taking up residence in the building in recent years.
All of the buildings come from Broome County tax foreclosure proceedings. The Land Bank meets regularly with Broome’s Real Property division to review which structures should be demolished rather than being put up for auction.
